Sirén: Ma Yuan “became a tai chao in the Academy during the reign of the Emperor Kuang Tsung”

bio.text: Ma Yuan (Japanese Ba-yen) flourished as a Court painter between 1190 and 1224. “In landscape, human figures, flowers, and birds, he was very successful, and stood first of the [Academicians].”
bio.lead: Herbert Giles, quoting a Chinese biography:

source.author: Herbert A. Giles
source.title: An Introduction to the History of Chinese Pictorial Art

bio.text: Ma Yuan was the most perfect product of a family of painters which had been active during several generations.
bio.lead: Osvald Sirén, on the Ma family of court painters:

source.author: Osvald Sirén
source.title: A History of Early Chinese Painting, vol. II

bio.text: His works, together with that of Xia Gui, formed the basis of the so-called Ma-Xia (馬夏) school of painting, and are considered among the finest from the period. His works has inspired both Chinese artists of the Zhe school, as well as the early Japanese painters Shūbun and Sesshū.
